podcast.body: Featured on the "Smash" album, this song contains the notable lyric "keep them separated." "Come out and play, keep them separated."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: The lyrics for this song were inspired by singer Dexter Holland's molecular biology lab work, where he realized he needed to keep Erlenmeyer Flasks containing hot bacteria samples "separated" to cool properly. The spoken word part was performed by Jason Blackpaw McClain, an Offspring superfan, as a thank you for his attendance at gigs and for his unique voice. The song was also subject to a plagiarism case due to an Arabic-sounding passage, but a musicologist ruled it was not a copy of Agent Orange's "Bloodstains," despite sharing an Arabian scale basis. "He thought to himself, I got to keep them separated."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
